definition: The central processing unit that executes instructions of a computer program.
The arithmetic logic unit that performs mathematical and logical operations.
A small high-speed memory location inside the CPU used to store immediate values.
Small, fast memory located close to the CPU used to speed up data access.
Volatile memory used to store data and programs currently in use.
Non-volatile memory that stores firmware and cannot be easily altered.
The main circuit board that connects and allows communication between hardware components.
A communication system that transfers data between components inside a computer.
The rate at which a CPU executes instructions, measured in GHz.
A device that allows a computer to interact with the outside world (keyboard, monitor, etc.).
A processor designed for graphics rendering and parallel computation.
A custom hardware chip built for a specific application.
A CPU design technique allowing overlapping execution of instructions.
Low-level software stored in ROM that provides hardware control functions.
The basic steps (fetch, decode, execute) executed by the CPU for each instruction.
